neighbours.label: ' of' / 'as' introducing the participants of a chemical reaction or relation (reaction of X with Y)
fire: Oxygen is released by the reaction of hydrogen peroxide with yeast.
Rust forms through the slow oxidation of iron in moist air.
Salt is produced by the neutralisation of an acid with a base.
The reaction of sodium with water gives off hydrogen gas.
Carbon dioxide comes from the combustion of methane in air.
The decomposition of calcium carbonate yields lime and carbon dioxide.
Energy is released during the fermentation of sugar by yeast.
The process is usually summarised as the conversion of glucose into ethanol.
quiet: Oxygen is released when hydrogen peroxide is poured onto yeast.
Rust forms slowly on iron that is left out in moist air.
Salt is produced when an acid is mixed with a base.
Sodium reacts violently with water and gives off hydrogen gas.
Carbon dioxide comes from methane burning in air.
Heating calcium carbonate yields lime and carbon dioxide.
Energy is released when yeast ferments sugar.
The process usually turns glucose into ethanol.

notes: Weak + pole (max 12.6) opposite a huge - pole on reaction arrows; logit effect suppresses arrows (->, =>). Top + tokens ' of' x5 in reaction descriptions.
